project: 2018 Toyota Yaris iA · TPMS + dual-camera blind-spot assist + 7" touch display
subtitle: Mazda2 DJ sedan blueprint · 100 × 100 mm 6-layer ESP32 carrier · Official 7" Touch Display + Raspberry Pi 4 in one printed enclosure

vehicle_blueprint.console_pocket_mm: 191 top × 123 bottom × 129 high (v1 paper fit); depth not measured: the enclosure needs ≥ 66 mm
vehicle_blueprint.display_mount_holes_mm: 4× M3 on 126.2 × 65.65 (frame flange) · 4× M2.5 on 58.0 × 49.0 (Pi standoffs)
vehicle_blueprint.carrier_pcb_mm: 100 × 100 × 1.6, 6 layers (JLCPCB: ENIG only, 0.5 oz inner copper) · 4× M3 on 92 × 92 (enclosure posts)
vehicle_blueprint.enclosure_mm: 205.6 × 127.9 × 71.8 (bezel to lid) · rear box 112 × 120, 60.5 behind the plate

console_float.name: Option A: console pocket (recommended)
console_float.summary: The printed enclosure sits in front of the console opening, upside down (cable edge up) for contrast when you look down at it. Its 205.6 × 127.9 mm bezel covers the 191 / 123 × 129 mm opening without climbing onto the HVAC panel. The 112 × 120 × 61 mm rear box with the Pi 4 and the carrier PCB drops into the pocket: it needs ≥ 66 mm of clear depth, and the car's USB / 12 V strip is behind it (measure with the foam mock-up). Air: chin intake → lid fan → 2 mm gap round the plate.
console_float.dsi_cable: stock 15-way ribbon: the Pi stays on the display's own standoffs
console_float.ergonomics: Low and shaded (cooler); you glance down. The amber LEDs at the mirrors and the pod's beep do the alerting.

dash_top.name: Option B: dash top on a RAM / AMPS mount
dash_top.summary: The same enclosure on a RAM-B-202U round base, screwed to the AMPS 30 × 38 mm M4 nuts in the box's bottom wall: an eye-level glance. More sun (250 cd/m² washes out) and heat (product brief: 0–50 °C), so take it in on hot days. Keep clear of the passenger airbag door and the windshield view.
dash_top.dsi_cable: stock 15-way ribbon: the Pi stays on the display's own standoffs
dash_top.ergonomics: Fastest glance; worst sun and heat.

v1_v2_pinout.v2: VSPI to the CC1101 (no OLED in v2)
Same: the v1 radio driver and EG53MA4 decoder are reused unchanged

v1_v2_pinout.v1: I2C SDA / SCL on J4 (4.7 k)
v1_v2_pinout.v2: I2C: optional VL6180X light sensor + LM75A board temperature
12 V active piezo in the alert pod (low-side MOSFET)
Mute / acknowledge button in the alert pod (same RC)
UART2 ↔ Pi GPIO14 / 15 (1 k / 4.7 k series; TX off while the Pi is unpowered)
Left / right blinker (PC817), polled at 1 kHz (errata 3.11). Earlier draft: IO35, which is the CC1101's GDO2
Left / right amber blind-spot LED (PWM, low-side MOSFET)
ACC sense, ADC1 (100 k / 10 k + clamp): key position and engine running (≥ 13 V)
GPS UART1 RX / TX (NEO-M8N, 9600 Bd): fallback speed for the speed gate (the OBD-II dongle first, over Bluetooth)
PI_INHIBIT: can only delay the Pi's regulator (pulled down: the Pi starts by default)
DevKit status LED; must be low at reset. Earlier draft: CAN RX, which idles high and breaks flashing

pcb6_stackup.role: Parts and signal routing. 5 V / 12 V currents in wide outer pours (inner copper is only 0.5 oz). Thermal reliefs on every through-hole pad
Solid ground plane under the whole board: reference for L1, ground under the CC1101 module
Low-current power distribution: 12V_PROT, 5V_ESP, 3V3 (the 5 A path stays on L1/L6)
Solid ground plane: shields the L5 signals from L3
Slow signals: blinker optos, Pi and GPS UARTs, I2C, SPI to the CC1101
Second high-current pour for 5V_PI / 12 V, stitched to L1; test pads; faces the Pi with a 3 mm air gap (pins ≤ 2.5 mm)

wiring_harness.name: Left mirror camera (USB UVC)
wiring_harness.route: Lower mirror cap, aimed back along the car's side → service loop through the mirror hinge → door harness → factory door boot (silicone grease) → kick panel → under the console trim → the Pi's USB 2.0 port through the enclosure's window (90° adapter)
wiring_harness.cable: The camera's own USB 2.0 lead (~3 m), not cut; or spliced with the pairs twisted and the shield continuous. No JST-GH in the data path
wiring_harness.protection: O-ring + neutral-cure RTV at the cap, drip loop, butyl on the door's vapour barrier, ferrite at the Pi

wiring_harness.name: Right mirror camera (USB UVC)
wiring_harness.route: Lower mirror cap → hinge service loop → passenger door harness → door boot → kick panel → behind the glovebox → the Pi's second USB 2.0 port (90° adapter)
wiring_harness.cable: The camera's own USB 2.0 lead (~3.5 m), same rules as the left

wiring_harness.name: 12 V ACC feed (one fuse tap)
wiring_harness.route: Driver's interior fuse box: Add-A-Circuit (5 A) on a non-critical ACC fuse, metered first (hot in ACC and ON, dead with the key out; never SRS or engine) → ring terminal on a chassis ground stud → under the dash → J1 Micro-Fit on the carrier, through the lid's cable exit
wiring_harness.protection: 4 A fuse + SMCJ22CA + P-MOSFET reverse protection + π filter on the board. ACC only: zero draw when parked, by construction

wiring_harness.name: 5 V / 5 A to the Pi and the display (inside the enclosure)
wiring_harness.route: J5 → 90° USB-C pigtail to the Pi; second pair → display adapter 5 V / GND; 2-pin header → lid fan
wiring_harness.protection: 470 µF at the Pi end; Pololu D36V50F5 (5.5 A); pass = vcgencmd get_throttled 0x0 under load

wiring_harness.name: Left / right turn-signal sense (IO36 / IO39)
wiring_harness.route: One 12 V lamp feed per side, found with the wiring diagram and a meter (kick panel, or the tail lamps) → solder or T-tap + heat-shrink → twisted pair → the PC817 inputs on the carrier
wiring_harness.protection: 2 × 1.1 kΩ + 1N4148 per input (~6 mA, isolated). Firmware bridges PWM gaps, rejects spikes and recognises hazards

wiring_harness.name: Pi ↔ ESP32 link (inside the enclosure)
wiring_harness.route: Pi GPIO14 / 15 + GND (90° Dupont) ↔ JST-GH on the carrier → UART2 IO16 / IO17
wiring_harness.protection: 1 k / 4.7 k series; the ESP32 keeps TX off while the Pi is unpowered; checksummed lines

wiring_harness.name: Left / right amber blind-spot LEDs
wiring_harness.route: Carrier JST-GH → with the camera cable through each door boot → LED in the inner door sail or mirror housing, facing the driver. Not in the A-pillar trim (curtain airbag)
wiring_harness.protection: Low-side MOSFET + series resistor; PWM level set by the Pi for night dimming. Steady = vehicle there, flashing = you are signalling towards it

wiring_harness.name: Alert pod: mute button + 12 V piezo
wiring_harness.route: Carrier JST-GH (4 pins: BTN, GND, BUZ+, BUZ−) → under the console trim → printed pod by the shifter (VHB + 2 screws). Not on the steering column or the knee bolster
wiring_harness.protection: 33 Ω + SMAJ18A on the 12 V feed; the v1 button RC. The button works with the Pi down: mute this turn, acknowledge a TPMS alarm

wiring_harness.name: GPS: fallback speed source (NEO-M8N)
wiring_harness.route: GPS puck on the dash top under the windshield (needs sky) → behind the instrument panel (not through the A-pillar trim) → carrier JST-GH (UART1 IO33 / IO27, 5 V)
wiring_harness.protection: Speed gate: the OBD-II speed first while the dongle answers, else GPS; both lost: last decision held 10 s, then LEDs only

wiring_harness.name: OBD-II speed: your Bluetooth dongle (optional)
wiring_harness.route: OBD-II port under the dash, driver's side → Bluetooth Classic → the ESP32 in the enclosure (no wires)
wiring_harness.cable: None: a low-profile dongle, or a short right-angle extension tied up out of the footwell
wiring_harness.protection: Requests PID 0x0D only, never listens to the bus; counts while < 1 s old, then the GPS takes over; parked drain measured first (B8). Not used for the blinker

wiring_harness.name: 315 MHz TPMS (4 × EG53MA4 → CC1101)
wiring_harness.route: CC1101's own SMA → 10 cm RG316 → SMA bulkhead in the enclosure wall → 30 cm RG316 → 315 MHz whip clear of the Pi, the display and the camera cables
wiring_harness.protection: 315 MHz-tuned CC1101 module; noise floor checked with everything on and off (bench test B6)

wiring_harness.name: Phase 2: CAN (no PCB change)
wiring_harness.route: OBD-II port → CANable-type USB adapter (gs_usb / SocketCAN) → a Pi USB port
wiring_harness.protection: Listen-only: never transmits. HS-CAN (pins 6/14): wheel speeds, gear, and the blinker broadcast 0x9A as a cross-check of the lamp taps (opendbc IDs, to confirm on this car)

power_budget.load: Official 7" Touch Display (docs: 200 mA at full brightness)
ESP32 DevKit (Bluetooth Classic link to the OBD dongle; Wi-Fi off)
CC1101 (via 3V3), GPS, LM75A, two amber LEDs

checklist_measure.text: PI_SEAT: glass front → top of the display's standoffs (enclosure parameter)
Pi orientation on the display: ports to the right seen from behind (the enclosure assumes it)
Thread depth of the display's 4 M3 frame holes (screws are M3 × 6 through a 3 mm plate)
Pushbutton thread (BUTTON_D) and the piezo's diameter / height (POD_BUZ_D / POD_BUZ_H)
Fan thickness and hole spacing (default 30 × 30 × 10, 24 mm)
Console pocket: clear depth where the box goes (≥ 66 mm), width at the box, position of the car's USB / 12 V strip
Mock-up in place: shifter P-R-N-D-M with your hand on it, HVAC knobs, view from the seat
ACC fuse: hot in ACC and ON, dead with the key out, behaviour during START
OBD dongle parked current at pin 16, key out, after 15 min (B8a): keep it plugged in only below ~5 mA
Turn-signal feeds: wire colours / pins from the wiring diagram, confirmed with a meter
Mirror cap: room for the camera barrel, drilling spot, cable path through the hinge
The four tyre IDs (rtl_433 -f 315M while driving)

checklist_bench.text: B1: Pololu EN delay (22 kΩ + 100 µF) at 12.6 V and 14.4 V
checklist_bench.where: Pass: 5 V after 1.3–1.6 s; nothing below ~7.5 V

checklist_bench.text: B2: inhibit through a 2N7002 + 100 Ω from 3.3 V
checklist_bench.where: Pass: off within ms, ~1.5 s restart

checklist_bench.text: B3: crank simulation 12.4 V 0.5 s → 0 V 1.5 s → 14.2 V
checklist_bench.where: Pass: the Pi starts only after the engine voltage

checklist_bench.text: B4: Pi + display + cameras + fan, CPU stress 30 min
B5: AM radio next to the running setup
B6: CC1101 noise floor with everything off, then on
B7: display upside down, image rotated 180°, touch inverted
checklist_bench.where: Pass: touch lands where you tap; better contrast from above

checklist_bench.text: B8: OBD dongle: parked current; ESP32 ↔ dongle over Bluetooth with the TPMS decoder running; optional ATCRA 09A sniff while signalling
checklist_bench.where: Pass: < ~5 mA parked; speed within ~3 s and matching the speedometer; TPMS decode rate unchanged

checklist_bench.text: T1: in the printed enclosure, in a sun-soaked car, vision app 30 min
Host tests and audits: test_logic (120 checks), check_pinmap.py (+ --selftest), make_enclosure.py (38 checks), sync_plan.py --check

checklist_tools.text: Plastic trim tools, 10 mm socket, Phillips #1 / #2, 2 mm and 2.5 mm hex keys
Micro-Fit crimper and a fine JST-GH crimper, or pre-crimped JST-GH leads
Soldering iron with a fine tip and a large tip (6-layer ground pads), flux, heat-shrink, heat gun
Step drill and a deburring tool for the mirror caps (practise on a spare cap)
Printer that does ASA / ABS (enclosed), or order MJF PA12

build_steps.text: Drive with rtl_433 -f 315M (wake each wheel with the OEC-T5) and log the four EG53MA4 tyre IDs; check the v1 decoder on the capture.
Display + Pi 4 on the bench: Bookworm, touch, brightness; rotate 180° and invert touch (B7).
Optional: identify your OBD-II dongle (Classic or BLE, PIN, MAC), read the speed with a phone app, measure its parked current (B8a). It feeds the speed gate only, never the blinker.
Two inventory USB cameras on the Pi: capture thread + 320 × 320 detector; measure the frame rate (V1) before buying car cameras.
Breadboard ESP32 + CC1101 + GPS + two blinker switches + piezo; run the v2 logic (120 host checks already pass) against the Pi over the UART protocol.
Print the fit template; tape the 112 × 120 × 61 mm foam block behind the glass outline; check the pocket, shifter and HVAC in the car (G5).
Measure PI_SEAT and the parts; regenerate (make_enclosure.py, 38 checks); print the bezel, then the housing, lid and pod in ASA; fit the display and the Pi (G6).
Breadboard the power path (fuse, SMCJ22CA, P-MOSFET, π filter, Pololu with the EN delay, TSR) from the ATX / LiPo 12 V: B1–B6 (G4).
KiCad layout inside the enclosure keep-outs (16 mm height, fan zone, SMA strip, pin-free corners); ERC / DRC 0 / 0, Gerber check, 1:1 print with the real parts (G7).
JLCPCB quote: confirm the 6-layer 100 × 100 promo and ENIG (G8); order 5.
Power the bare board from the bench at 12.0–14.4 V; check the rails, the EN delay and the inhibit before fitting the Pi; then the ESP32 and the CC1101; noise floor with everything on (B6).
Cameras into the mirror caps (O-ring + neutral-cure RTV); cables through the hinges and door boots with service loops; reseal the vapour barriers with butyl; LEDs in the door sails.

One Add-A-Circuit on the metered ACC fuse + chassis ground; blinker feeds from the wiring diagram; GPS on the dash top (fallback speed); the OBD dongle in its port if it passed B8; alert pod by the shifter.
Enclosure into the pocket (or onto the RAM base): 90° USB adapters, harness through the grommet, antenna lead out; never seal the gap round the plate.
Mark the blind-spot zones on the touch screen with a car parked in each lane; check the mirror-alignment reference; T1 thermal test in a hot car.
Read-only root on; road test by day, at night, on the highway, in rain and in a parking lot (quiet below 8 mph); all four tyres reporting.

premortem.title: HS-CAN on ESP32 GPIO2 plus an MCP2515 on IO15 for MS-CAN
premortem.cause: GPIO2 must be low at reset or serial flashing fails, and a CAN receiver idles high. The MCP2515 also needs an interrupt pin, and no pins were left
premortem.fix: CAN moves to a USB CAN adapter (CANable / gs_usb) on the Pi in phase 2: SocketCAN, listen-only, no PCB change

premortem.title: Power latch from 12 V BAT with an "OR gate" and a "30 s hardware watchdog"
premortem.cause: Never designed; a stuck latch flattens the battery, and the ESP32 controlled the Pi's power
premortem.fix: ACC-only power (P1). No latch, no battery tap, zero draw parked by construction. A read-only root makes hard power-off safe

premortem.title: The ESP32 enables the Pi rail
premortem.cause: Flashing the ESP32 from the Pi resets it, the rail drops, the Pi dies mid-flash: deadlock
premortem.fix: The Pi regulator is on by default with ACC (Pololu EN has an internal 100 kΩ pull-up). The ESP32 can only delay it (PIN_PI_INHIBIT, pulled down)

premortem.title: Pololu D36V50F5 treated as a 36 V part
premortem.cause: Pololu's page: 5.5–50 V in, reverse protection to 40 V, ~5.5 A, EN on by default, 3 A per header pin
premortem.fix: Kept, with its real ratings. Power pins on both header rows (6 A per pair)

premortem.title: 1.5KE24CA TVS
premortem.cause: Minimum breakdown 22.8 V: it conducts on a 24 V jump start and burns
premortem.fix: SMCJ22CA: 24.4 V minimum breakdown, 35.5 V clamp, 1500 W. Same choice as the v1 audit, sized up

premortem.title: (implied) series Schottky for reverse polarity
premortem.cause: ~1 W at 2.5 A in an SMA package
premortem.fix: P-MOSFET reverse protection (−40 V, ≤ 20 mΩ, e.g. AOD4185) with a 12 V gate clamp

premortem.title: Blind-spot LEDs in the "A-pillar mirror-sail triangles, zero door-boot wires"
premortem.cause: The Yaris iA has side-curtain airbags behind the A-pillar trim, and the triangle at the mirror base belongs to the door
premortem.fix: LEDs on the inner door sail or in the mirror housing, wired with the camera cable through the door boot. Nothing in the A-pillar trim or on the dash top

premortem.title: Piezo under the steering-column lower shroud
premortem.cause: Next to the collapsible column and the knee-bolster area
premortem.fix: In the alert pod with the mute button, near the shifter: one 4-wire lead

premortem.title: Bi-colour amber/red LEDs
premortem.cause: Red light near the windshield is a legal grey zone and isn't the OEM convention
premortem.fix: Amber only: steady = vehicle in the blind spot, flashing = you are signalling towards it

premortem.title: "50 Ω microstrip from the CC1101 to an SMA" on the PCB
premortem.cause: The module has its own SMA; there is no RF trace
premortem.fix: Module at the board edge with its SMA overhanging; ground plane under it

premortem.title: Pi 4 M2.5 hole pattern (58 × 49 mm) so the PCB can stack behind the Pi
premortem.cause: Those holes land under the ESP32 DevKit and the CC1101, and stacking blocks the Pi's fan and USB
premortem.fix: Dropped from rev A; 4 × M3 on 92 × 92 mm only

premortem.title: The 7" display "floats in the pocket and clears the shifter"
premortem.cause: The glass is 192.96 mm wide; the opening is 191 mm at the top and 132.6 mm at the glass's bottom edge
premortem.fix: It can only sit in front of the trim, overhanging ~30 mm per side. Decide with the 1:1 mock-up

premortem.title: The display is "in inventory"
premortem.cause: The inventory lists only the Touch Display Adapter v1.1 board
premortem.fix: Confirm the LCD glass, touch panel and both ribbons exist (G3)

premortem.title: Blinker inputs on IO36 / IO39 as interrupts
premortem.cause: ESP32 errata 3.11: these pins glitch low for ~80 ns when the ADC or Wi-Fi powers up
premortem.fix: Polled at 1 kHz with an RC filter (poll tag, enforced by the audit)

premortem.title: "Mirror LED turn signals" on the Yaris iA (drawn in the viewer)
premortem.cause: Not verified
premortem.fix: Check your mirrors; the plan no longer depends on them

premortem.title: v2 still listed the v1 front-panel controls (EC11 encoder, menu buttons) plus a "camera toggle" button
premortem.cause: The 7" touch screen does menus, settings, TPMS pairing and camera calibration; the 2.7" OLED and the 4 tyre LEDs are redundant too
premortem.fix: All removed. One mute/acknowledge button stays (IO4, same RC as v1), in the alert pod with the buzzer: it works while the Pi is down, and you can find it without looking

premortem.title: Our own fit template placed the display's M3 holes 0.65 mm off
premortem.cause: The drawing dimensions them from the outer frame flange (11.89 line), not the frame body (12.54)
premortem.fix: Fixed: x = 34.87 / 161.07 mm (front view), now centred on the flange. Template regenerated; the enclosure uses the same values

premortem.title: Display "0–50 °C, brightness not specified"
premortem.cause: The product brief's safety notes say 0–50 °C; the documentation page lists −20 to +70 °C operating, −30 to +80 °C storage, 250 cd/m², 500:1, viewing 50° top / 70° bottom
premortem.fix: Design for the brief; 250 cd/m² is dim in daylight (D2); the viewing angles confirm the upside-down mount (D3)

premortem.title: "The Pi's USB end can face either side"
premortem.cause: The docs photo shows the documented way: GPIO on top and ports to the right, seen from behind
premortem.fix: The enclosure is built for it (ports to the driver's right when mounted upside down). Turned round, 2 fit checks fail

premortem.title: Phase 2: "HS-CAN speed/reverse, MS-CAN turn signals"
premortem.cause: For the 2016–21 Mazdas that openpilot supports, the turn lamps (BLINK_INFO, 0x9A) and the stalk (TURN_SWITCH, 0x91) are on the powertrain HS-CAN, next to the speed (ENGINE_DATA, 0x202). This car uses that message family: Metasploit's mazda_ic_mover drives the Mazda 2 / Scion iA / Yaris iA cluster with one 0x202 frame
premortem.fix: Phase 2 listens on HS-CAN (OBD pins 6/14). The IDs come from opendbc's reverse-engineered mazda_2017.dbc: confirm each one on this car (B8) before relying on it

premortem.title: The key passes through ACC on the way to START; the Pi starts booting and the crank browns it out, or it boot-loops
premortem.fix: Pololu EN RC delay (22 kΩ + 100 µF: ~1.3–1.6 s at 12.6–14.4 V, no start below ~7.5 V). Firmware holds the Pi until the engine runs (≥ 13.0 V for 1 s) or 15 s in ACC

premortem.title: Battery flat after a week parked
premortem.fix: ACC-only power: nothing is connected when the key is out

premortem.title: SD card corrupted by hard power-off
premortem.fix: Read-only root (raspi-config overlay FS), journal in RAM, settings in ESP32 NVS, a high-endurance card

premortem.title: 5 V sags under load: undervoltage flag, USB cameras drop out
premortem.fix: 5.5 A regulator, 18 AWG under 0.5 m, 470 µF at the Pi end; budget ~2.4 A typical, ~3.8 A peak. Pass = get_throttled 0x0 after a 30-minute load test

premortem.title: Load dump, jump start, reverse battery or negative spikes kill the board
premortem.fix: Onboard 4 A fuse + SMCJ22CA + P-MOSFET; downstream ratings TSR 1-2450 36 V, Pololu 50 V, MOSFET 40 V. A load dump above 35 V on a car without central suppression is an accepted trade-off (as in v1)

premortem.title: AM radio buzz: the ~500 kHz regulator's harmonics fall in the AM band
premortem.fix: π filter (ferrite + 2.2 µH + 2 × 10 µF) on 12 V, short twisted leads, ferrites. Test with the AM radio. Rev B could use a 2.1 MHz automotive buck

premortem.title: A fuse tap on the wrong fuse (SRS, engine ECU) or the wrong way round
premortem.fix: One Add-A-Circuit, 5 A, on a non-critical ACC fuse. Meter it: hot in ACC and ON, dead with the key out; note whether it drops in START. Never a yellow SRS circuit

premortem.title: Hand-soldering a 6-layer board: through-hole pins on inner planes won't wet
premortem.fix: Thermal reliefs on all plane connections; ENIG

premortem.title: 5 A on 0.5 oz inner copper overheats
premortem.fix: High-current paths as ≥ 3 mm outer-layer pours with stitching vias

premortem.title: The ESP32 back-powers an unpowered Pi through the UART
premortem.fix: 1 k / 4.7 k series resistors; firmware keeps UART TX off while the Pi rail is off

premortem.title: Opto resistors overheat on a load dump
premortem.fix: 2 × 1.1 kΩ 1206 in series per input (0.5 W), 1N4148 reverse diode

premortem.likelihood: High (the earlier drafts did it twice)
premortem.title: A strapping pin is misused: GPIO12 high at reset (wrong flash voltage), GPIO2 high (flashing fails)
premortem.fix: Pin map audit with rules for strapping, input-only, flash, boot-glitch, ADC1 and UART0 pins

premortem.title: Opening /dev/ttyUSB0 toggles DTR/RTS and resets the ESP32
premortem.fix: The runtime link is the GPIO UART (Pi GPIO14/15 ↔ ESP32 UART2); USB is only for flashing. The Pi's power no longer depends on the ESP32

premortem.title: The Pi's UART carries Bluetooth or a login console
premortem.fix: enable_uart=1, dtoverlay=disable-bt, remove console=serial0,... from cmdline.txt

premortem.title: Garbage, partial lines or a corrupted message trigger a wrong alert
premortem.fix: NMEA-style lines with XOR checksum, strict field parsing, resync on $, overlong lines dropped

premortem.title: A ground offset or noise between the boards corrupts the UART
premortem.fix: Common star ground at the regulator; 115200 Bd over < 1 m

premortem.title: Pi 4 too slow for two streams plus YOLO
premortem.fix: 320 × 320 NCNN, alternate sides, blinker side first, hardware JPEG decode; fall back to motion-in-ROI. Measure in phase 1 with the two USB cameras you already have, before buying cameras

premortem.title: The Pi 4 has 1 GB of RAM
premortem.fix: free -h; need ≥ 2 GB

premortem.title: The Pi throttles in a hot cabin, worse inside a closed enclosure
premortem.fix: Enclosure airflow: chin intake slots → past the Pi and round the PCB → 30 mm lid fan (inventory) blowing out → a 2 mm gap round the plate (bumps), so the pocket is never sealed. Heatsinks; hot-start hold (board ≥ 60 °C: wait for 55 °C, at most 10 min). Test T1 in a sun-soaked car: SoC < 80 °C, get_throttled = 0x0. If it fails: lower clock, bigger gap, or the PCB in its own box

premortem.title: No small USB camera fits under the mirror (most "mirror cameras" are analog/AHD)
premortem.fix: Acceptance criteria before buying: UVC MJPEG 720p30, WDR (Starvis), no IR LEDs, −20…+70 °C, IP67, barrel ≤ 20 mm, ≥ 3 m cable, 90–110° lens. Fallback: AHD cameras + a 2-channel USB capture. Measure the barrel before drilling

premortem.title: Cutting the USB cable for the door boot breaks USB 2.0 high-speed
premortem.fix: No JST-GH in the data path: splice with the pairs kept twisted and the shield continuous, or a solder-type USB-A plug. Pass = no resets in dmesg on a 30-minute drive

premortem.title: A folded or bumped mirror points the camera elsewhere; the blind-spot zone is wrong
premortem.fix: At start-up the Pi compares the car-body edge with the stored reference; on mismatch it sets camFault for that side → fault pattern on that LED, no alerts from that side
premortem.status: Fixed (protocol + ESP32 logic); Pi side to implement

premortem.title: Night, rain or low sun hides vehicles; motorcycles are tiny
premortem.fix: Starvis WDR, no IR LEDs, hydrophobic lens coating, headlight-blob fallback in the ROI, lower motorcycle threshold with persistence

premortem.title: The vision app crashes or freezes and the system fails silently
premortem.fix: systemd Restart=always + watchdog on the Pi; the ESP32 shows the fault pattern and gives one fault beep after 1 s without a fresh report

premortem.title: 20–35 s boot: no blind-spot help just after starting
premortem.fix: Lamp test when the system becomes ready, so you know when it works

premortem.title: OpenCV / NCNN / Python dependency breakage on a later image
premortem.fix: Pinned versions, a provisioning script, a golden SD-card image

premortem.title: The display is damaged by a parked car's heat
premortem.fix: Ratings disagree (brief 0–50 °C, docs −20…+70 °C operating, −30…+80 °C storage): design for the brief. Shaded console mount preferred, sunshade, AMPS quick-release for heat waves, hot-start hold

premortem.title: Washed out in sunlight: the docs give only 250 cd/m² and 500:1
premortem.fix: Shaded mount; the bezel lip shades the border; full backlight by day; high-contrast UI (white on black, large icons). Test in the sun with the mock-up

premortem.title: Poor contrast from the driver's seat
premortem.fix: 6 o'clock viewing direction; the docs give 50° from the top, 70° from the bottom. Looking down at it: mount it upside down (the enclosure's default, MOUNT=inverted). Rotate the image 180° (Screen Configuration → Inverted, or in the app); touch: dtoverlay=vc4-kms-dsi-7inch,invx,invy

premortem.title: The screen and LEDs glare at night
premortem.fix: LED level sent by the Pi (from camera exposure); backlight dimming; optional VL6180X light sensor on I2C

premortem.title: Distraction: touching the screen while driving
premortem.fix: Nothing needs touch while moving; camera view only on blinker or danger; the one action you need while driving (mute) is the physical pod button

premortem.title: A video screen visible to the driver is illegal
premortem.fix: Camera views for manoeuvring are generally allowed (e.g. California VC 27602(b)(4)); no entertainment video. Check your state

premortem.title: Touch-only controls: no way to silence an alarm while the Pi boots (20–35 s) or after it crashes; gloves
premortem.fix: Mute/acknowledge button in the alert pod, wired to the ESP32 (IO4), which also drives the buzzer and the TPMS logic on its own

premortem.title: Phantom touches or a cracked glass from a bezel that presses on it
premortem.fix: The display hangs on its own 4 × M3 frame holes; the lip sits 0.3 mm clear of the glass and only over the black border, outside the touch area

premortem.title: The display doesn't fit: shifter in P/R/N/D/M, your hand, the HVAC knobs
premortem.fix: 1:1 template + a foam block the size of the enclosure's rear box. The bezel is 127.9 mm tall, under the 129 mm opening, so it doesn't climb onto the HVAC panel (checked by the generator)

premortem.title: The enclosure's rear box (112 × 120 × 61 mm) is deeper than the pocket or hits the car's USB/12 V strip, which sits behind the panel ~34 mm below the top of the opening
premortem.fix: Measure ≥ 66 mm clear depth with the mock-up. If not: the car's USB moves to a passthrough, or the PCB goes in its own box (same 92 × 92 posts) and the enclosure shrinks to ~45 mm

premortem.title: Printed parts warp or creep in the heat
premortem.fix: You can print: ASA or ABS (enclosed printer), PETG only in the shaded console, never PLA (soft at ~55–60 °C). Or MJF PA12 from JLC3DP with the PCB

premortem.title: The display comes loose in a crash or on bumps
premortem.fix: The display bolts to the housing through its own M3 frame holes; the housing bolts to the car via the AMPS M4 nuts or a pocket bracket, never tape only; no sharp edges; nothing in airbag zones

premortem.title: Vibration loosens sockets and connectors
premortem.fix: Latching connectors (Micro-Fit, JST-GH), strain relief, machined sockets + a dab of RTV (v1 rule), nylon lock nuts

premortem.title: Cracking the mirror cap while drilling
premortem.fix: Practise on a used mirror cap; step drill; measure the camera barrel first

premortem.title: Water in the camera, the door or the footwell
premortem.fix: O-ring + neutral-cure (oxime) RTV, drip loop, silicone grease only on the boot, reseal the door's vapour barrier with butyl after routing

premortem.title: Cables break in the mirror hinge or the door boot
premortem.fix: Service loop, follow the factory harness, cycle door / window / mirror 50 times after the install

premortem.title: Cables snag the pedals, the steering column or the seat rails
premortem.fix: Tie them up high along existing harnesses; never splice into the yellow SRS harness

premortem.title: The enclosure is drawn from estimates: the Pi seat height isn't in any drawing; straight Dupont plugs stand ~22 mm on the Pi's GPIO and would hit the PCB
premortem.fix: PI_SEAT and PI_TOP_H are parameters: measure, regenerate, and the 38 checks re-run. Use 90° or low-profile GPIO housings. Print the bezel first (~2 h) as a fit test

premortem.title: Screws into the display's frame bottom out and press on the panel
premortem.fix: M3 × 6 through a 3 mm plate; check the thread depth first

premortem.title: Fingers reach the boards through vents (Raspberry Pi docs: the enclosure must make the boards unreachable)
premortem.fix: Chin slots 2.5 mm; fan grille with 2.5 mm gaps; split grommet in the cable exit

premortem.title: The camera USB plugs and the antenna lead don't fit beside the box in the pocket
premortem.fix: 90° USB-A adapters and an SMA bulkhead; the generator checks plugs (+15 mm) and the lead inside the opening's outline (1.3 mm margin at the tightest point)

premortem.title: No 12 V turn-signal wire found at the kick panel
premortem.fix: Get the wiring diagram (the Yaris iA is in Toyota's service information, techinfo.toyota.com, short subscriptions) and confirm with a meter. Fallback: the tail-lamp feeds in the trunk. Phase 2: CAN

premortem.title: The body control module drives the lamps with PWM; a simple input sees noise
premortem.fix: The detector bridges PWM gaps up to 25 ms and needs 50 ms to count, so PWM reads as a steady flash and spikes are ignored

premortem.title: Hazards cause a danger beep (both sides look like turns)
premortem.fix: Hazards are recognised when both sides light within 150 ms; a single side is reported only after that window, and after hazards end only after a fresh flash

premortem.title: The added load trips bulb-out detection (fast flash)
premortem.fix: Each opto input draws ~6 mA

premortem.title: Our electronics desensitise the 315 MHz key fob receiver
premortem.fix: ACC-only: everything is off when you use the fob

premortem.title: CAN not on the OBD port, or behind a gateway
premortem.fix: Doesn't matter for the speed: OBD-II requires every car to answer standard requests such as PID 0x0D at the port. Only the phase-2 CAN cross-check needs the broadcasts on pins 6/14: check with a filtered sniff (B8)

premortem.title: The blinker is read from the dongle instead of the lamp wires, and a dropped Bluetooth link looks like "not signalling": no danger beep, silently
premortem.fix: Standard OBD-II has no turn-signal data; the lamps exist only as a Mazda-private broadcast (0x9A). The blinker stays on the opto taps (G9); OBD is used for the speed only. A CAN blinker is at most a phase-2 cross-check on a wired, listen-only adapter

premortem.title: The ELM327 is asked to listen to the bus (AT MA) and overflows
premortem.fix: Datasheet: a 512-byte buffer, and at the 38.4 kbaud a typical Bluetooth clone uses inside, printing one frame takes ~5.2 ms, while a 40 %-loaded 500 kbit/s bus delivers one every ~0.35 ms: BUFFER FULL. Monitoring also blocks requests. The firmware only *requests* PID 0x0D (010D1), one at a time

premortem.title: The dongle sleeps, hangs, answers ? or NO DATA, or the link drops; the speed goes stale
premortem.fix: 1 s timeouts, a reset (ATZ) after 3 failures, plain 010D for clones without the response-count digit, reconnect. OBD speed counts only while < 1 s old; then the GPS takes over, then the 10 s hold, then LEDs only. A bad dongle can only make the buzzer quieter

premortem.title: Flat battery: the dongle is powered from OBD pin 16, always on. ELM327 datasheet: "about as much current as a dome lamp" (29.8 mA for its reference circuit, 17.6 mA in low-power mode)
premortem.fix: Measure its parked current (B8). Keep it plugged in only if it sleeps below ~5 mA; otherwise unplug it when parked for days, or use an OBD extension with a switch

premortem.title: Anyone in Bluetooth range connects with the default PIN and injects CAN frames: mazda_ic_mover moves this car's cluster needles with one 0x202 frame
premortem.fix: A dongle that needs a button press to pair, or sleeps its radio when parked; change the PIN if it allows; unplug it for long parking. The ESP32 itself only sends the setup AT commands and 010D

premortem.title: Bluetooth on the ESP32 disturbs the 315 MHz decoder's edge interrupt or the 1 kHz loop
premortem.fix: Bluetooth stack on core 0; the RF edge interrupt (rf_capture.cpp) and the 1 kHz loop on core 1. B8 compares the TPMS decode rate with the link on and off

premortem.title: The Pi would be the natural Bluetooth host, but its Bluetooth is off (dtoverlay=disable-bt: the PL011 UART carries the ESP32 link)
premortem.fix: The ESP32 talks to the dongle: the WROOM-32 has Bluetooth Classic. Connect by MAC address (a name search takes seconds), PIN usually 1234 or 0000. No change on the Pi or the PCB

premortem.title: The dongle is BLE-only (if it works with an iPhone, it is BLE or Wi-Fi), so Bluetooth Classic serial can't reach it
premortem.fix: Identify it first. The client logic doesn't depend on the transport: a BLE dongle needs a GATT client (NimBLE) instead of BluetoothSerial; a Wi-Fi one is out (the ESP32's Wi-Fi stays off)

premortem.title: A long dongle or an extension at the driver's knee catches a foot or a knee
premortem.fix: Low-profile dongle, or a short right-angle extension tied up out of the footwell

premortem.title: The 433 MHz-tuned CC1101 module loses up to ~10 dB at 315 MHz; rear wheels drop out
premortem.fix: Buy a 315 MHz-tuned CC1101 module with the same 2 × 4 pinout (~$3); keep the 433 one as a spare. Check RSSI per wheel

premortem.title: The Pi 4, its USB 3 ports, the display and the regulator raise the 315 MHz noise floor
premortem.fix: The antenna leaves the enclosure: CC1101 → short RG316 → SMA bulkhead in the box wall → 30 cm RG316 → whip away from the Pi; cameras on the USB 2.0 ports; ferrites. Compare the noise floor with everything on and off

premortem.title: The EG53MA4 decoder fails on real frames
premortem.fix: Not yet tested on a real capture: drive with rtl_433 -f 315M first (v1 premortem step 1)

premortem.title: Nuisance alerts in parking lots, drive-thrus and queues
premortem.fix: No alerts below 8 mph, on again at 12 mph (hysteresis); hazards silent; the mute button silences the current turn only; at most one danger beep per 3 s, and a flickering detection can't beep more than once a second

premortem.title: GPS lost under a bridge or in a tunnel: alerts stop or go wild
premortem.fix: The car's own speed from the OBD dongle covers tunnels, garages and GPS cold starts. Without both, the last moving/slow decision is held 10 s; after that the LEDs keep working and the buzzer stays quiet

premortem.title: Trusting it: a missed motorcycle at night
premortem.fix: It is an aid: always look over your shoulder. Disclaimer on the start screen

premortem.title: A silent failure looks like "all clear"
premortem.fix: Fault pattern + one beep on a lost Pi link; per-side fault for a camera

premortem.title: The blind-spot beep is drowned out by a TPMS reminder or vice versa
premortem.fix: Priorities: danger, then fault, then TPMS; TPMS repeats at most every 10 minutes

premortem.title: Scope creep: the project never finishes
premortem.fix: Ship in useful steps: (1) the camera view switches on the blinker, no AI; (2) detection, LEDs and buzzer; (3) CAN and the 60 GHz radar

premortem.title: Footprint errors (Pololu module, DevKit, connectors)
premortem.fix: Print the layout 1:1 and set the real parts on it before ordering, as for v1

premortem.title: Inventory entries are wrong or incomplete
premortem.fix: Collect every part before the layout freeze (G3)

premortem.title: Tools missing for the car work
premortem.fix: Multimeter, trim tools, fine crimper for JST-GH (or pre-crimped leads), solder-type USB-A plugs, step drill, heat gun: see the tools checklist in the viewer

premortem.title: The enclosure becomes the long pole (~12 h of printing per try, ASA needs an enclosed printer)
premortem.fix: Parametric generator with fit checks; print the bezel first; foam mock-up before any printing; MJF PA12 as the no-printer route

order_gate.needed: Electrical spec frozen; pin map passes the audit
order_gate.detail: Done: pins_v2.h, python 01-hardware/v2/check_pinmap.py → 0 errors, its self-test catches all six earlier pin errors

order_gate.needed: Safety logic written and unit-tested (power-up, blinker, alerts, Pi link, OBD-II speed)
order_gate.detail: Done: 02-firmware/v2, 120 host checks pass; removing the hazard fixes, the TPMS acknowledge or the OBD fallbacks makes them fail

order_gate.needed: Every part physically on hand and identified
order_gate.detail: You: 7" LCD glass + touch + both ribbons (the inventory lists only the adapter board), Pi 4 RAM ≥ 2 GB, CC1101 module pinout, GPS cable pinout, Pololu D36V50F5 bought

order_gate.needed: Power path breadboarded: EN delay, inhibit, crank dip, 4 A load, vcgencmd get_throttled = 0x0
Display location chosen with the 1:1 mock-up (Option A console or B dash top)
order_gate.detail: You: print v2_fit_template_1to1.pdf, tape a 112 × 120 × 61 mm foam block behind the glass outline (the enclosure's rear box), check ≥ 66 mm of pocket depth, the shifter, the HVAC knobs and the car's USB/12 V strip

order_gate.needed: PI_SEAT measured and the enclosure regenerated; bezel and housing test-printed and fitted to the real display and Pi
order_gate.detail: You: 1 measurement + ~12 h of printing. The PCB's keep-outs (fan zone, SMA strip, corners, 16 mm height) come from this

order_gate.needed: KiCad schematic and layout inside the enclosure's keep-outs, ERC/DRC 0/0, independent Gerber check, footprints printed 1:1 and test-fitted with the real parts
order_gate.detail: Next step, after G3–G6 (generator based on the v1 build script)

order_gate.needed: JLCPCB quote confirms the 6-layer 100 × 100 mm promo price and options
order_gate.detail: You, at checkout. Verified from JLCPCB's capability page: 6+ layer FR-4 is ENIG only (no HASL), inner copper is 0.5 oz by default

pcb_constraints.outline: 100 × 100 mm, parts face the lid, 4× M3 on 92 × 92 into the posts
pcb_constraints.fan_zone: 32 × 32 mm centred at template [45.0, 46.0] (mm from the top-left, parts side up): parts ≤ 6 mm
pcb_constraints.sma_strip: 14 mm into the board × 12 mm along the edge, on the edge away from the Pi's ports, centred 34.5 mm below the board's top edge: no parts
pcb_constraints.corners: 10 × 10 mm round each mounting hole: no through-hole pins (posts and ribs underneath)

hardware.display_to_plate: 4× M3 × 6 button head (check how deep the display's threads are first)
hardware.fan: 30 mm 5 V fan from the black Pi case, 4× M3 × 16 + nuts, blowing OUT through the lid
hardware.amps: 4× M4 nuts in the bottom bosses, M4 × 10 (RAM-B-202U round base, or a car bracket)
hardware.pod: 2× M3 × 8, VHB tape under the base
